newsitem.title: USA: Oregon sets Feb 14 hearing on Enron merger.
newsitem.headline: Oregon sets Feb 14 hearing on Enron merger.

text.p: The Oregon Public Utilities Commission (OPUC) will hold a special hearing February 14 on the proposed merger of Enron Corp and Portland General Electric Co, a spokesman for OPUC in Salem said Friday.
The meeting was called after a three-day settlement conference this week failed to result in a compromise between the commission staff and the companies on terms of the merger.
"There was no meeting of the minds here," the commission spokesman said.
He explained that the commission staff's estimate of cost savings from the merger of more than $47 million a year is far apart from Enron and PGE's $3-million estimate.
A spokesman for Enron in Houston said the purpose of the February meeting will be to ask the commission members to give the staff and interested parties more guidance on policy issues.
"We are encouraged that we can continue talks," the OPUC spokesman said.
The Oregon commission still expects to meet a March 17 deadline for deciding on the merger plan, he added.
